correctness.rationale: For p,q≥2t+3, same-part pairs have at least three common opposite neighbors, hence those are forced into every geodesic hull. If a proper convex set contains a≥2 left vertices, it subsequently contains b≥3 right and a≥3 left. Outside vertices have at most one neighbor inside each opposite side; this gives (q-b)(a-1)≤at and (p-a)(b-1)≤bt, together with a,b≤t+1, leading to incompatible lower/upper bounds on q-b. Thus proper convex sets are ∅, singletons, or edge pairs. The VC=2 and Littlestone=3 claims follow by direct combinatorial version-space shattering and upper bound. At p=q=2t+2 the explicit partitioned missing-edge pattern leaves a proper convex K2,2, establishing sharpness. Independently calculated 32 convex sets on the 5×5 crown graph, confirming edge+singleton+two count; finite check is corroborative only.
